# stablr: Sparse and Reliable Biomarker Discovery in R

### R-native STABL: sparse, stable biomarker selection with false-discovery calibration

The `stablr` package implements STABL (Stability-based Thresholding and
Aggregation for Biomarker discovery via LASSO) for high-dimensional
clinical and omic data. The method repeats three steps. It resamples the
data. It fits a sparse learner across a penalty grid. It records how
often each feature is selected. It then calibrates these selection
frequencies against artificial decoy features. The package keeps the
parity-critical STABL semantics of the Python implementation. It exposes
R-native S3 objects, `glmnet`-ecosystem learners, multi-omic workflows,
visualization helpers, and CSV/disk export utilities. It compiles C++
but has no Python or tidymodels runtime dependency.

Major functionality of `stablr`:

- [`stabl()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl.html)
                      Simple selector: a data.frame in, a plain-language
  selection out
- [`stabl_fit()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_fit.html)
                     Expert interface: full control of lambda grid,
  bootstrap design, thresholds, and learners
- [`compute_fdp_plus()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/compute_fdp_plus.html)
                FDP+ thresholding with random-permutation and knockoff
  artificial features
- [`stabl_multiomic_train_validate()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_multiomic_train_validate.html)
  Multi-omic train/validation with early, late, and cooperative fusion
- [`stabl_multiomic_nested_cv()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_multiomic_nested_cv.html)
      Outer CV with sample-i.i.d., grouped, or study-disjoint folds
- [`stabl_multiomic_scheme_comparison()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_multiomic_scheme_comparison.html)
  Compare CV schemes arm-by-arm on held-out error
- [`stabl_environment_stability()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_environment_stability.html)
  Transportable selections across environments (experimental)
- [`jaccard_similarity_matrix()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/jaccard_similarity_matrix.html)
     Selection-reproducibility metrics

## Motivation

A high-dimensional biomarker screen begins with an uncomfortable fact:
there are many more tempting variables than there are samples. A sparse
model can still choose a short list. But a single fit does not tell
whether the list is sturdy or merely lucky. A selection that reproduces
only inside its own sampling scheme has little value for a new cohort or
a new lab.

STABL turns the one-shot question into a repeated experiment. Bootstrap
resampling paired with artificial decoy features converts selection
frequency into a calibrated decision. A feature is retained only when it
out-competes decoys that carry no signal. The fitted threshold is the
first minimizer of the observed FDP+ diagnostic curve. `stablr` extends
the same discipline across omic views (early, late, and cooperative
fusion) and across environments and studies (grouped and study-disjoint
resampling), so that reliability and transportability are measured
rather than assumed.

## stablr workflow

![stablr workflow](reference/figures/workflow.png)

### Analysis modes

[`stabl_analyze()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_analyze.md)
makes the evidence level explicit via a required `mode` argument.
`mode = "exploratory"` fits STABL on the full data and returns a
canonical interpretation table
([`stabl_interpret()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_interpret.md))
labelled `post_selection_descriptive` — coefficients, stability, effect
directions, and correlation groups describe the fitting data and are not
predictive evidence. `mode = "validated"` runs nested cross-validation
with fold-fitted preprocessing
([`stabl_preprocess_fit()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_preprocess_fit.md)
/
[`stabl_preprocess_apply()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_preprocess_apply.md))
and returns held-out predictions, pooled and per-repeat performance, and
held-out permutation importance labelled `cross_validated`. Binary
outcomes report accuracy, balanced error rate, macro-F1, MCC, Brier,
log-loss, and AUROC; gaussian outcomes report MAE, RMSE, and R² (with
explicit definitions — negative R² is retained, and an empty selection
falls back to a deterministic intercept-only model). A validated
analysis with `final_refit = TRUE` can be packed into a portable final
model with
[`stabl_finalize()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_finalize.md)
and applied to new data with
[`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html).

Evidence status (simulation-only, predeclared gates,
`benchmarks/iv_summary.md`): effect-direction recovery 1.00; null
validated AUROC centred at chance (median 0.473); leaky full-data
selection is directionally optimistic over nested validation (+0.015
mean AUROC); one-feature folds produce non-degenerate probabilities. One
predeclared criterion was NOT met: correlated substitutes are always
assigned to a single correlation group when co-selected, but FDP+
selection retains all members of a correlated block in only 60% of runs
— do not expect complete co-selection of redundant features. Multiclass
and ordinal graduation remain reserved (WS-9 ordinal graduation NOT
met).

## Technical intro

`stablr` is R-native without a Python runtime. The core STABL method is
parity-tested against the Python STABL implementation (Hédou et
al. 2024); cross-language solver validation uses ranking/support
contracts and does not claim bit-identical coefficients. The
cooperative-learning backend is compiled C++17 (vendored multiview
engine), and learners come from the `glmnet` ecosystem: lasso, elastic
net, adaptive lasso, and optional sparse group lasso, with gaussian,
binomial, multinomial, and Cox outcomes where the backend supports the
family. A random-forest learner (`ranger`) and an ordinal-regression
learner (`ordinalNet`) are also available as base learners.

The interface is two-tier.
[`stabl()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl.md) runs
STABL with statistically safe defaults — model-X knockoff artificial
features, FDP+ calibration, strict fallback, automatic lambda grid — and
prints a plain-language answer:

``` r

library(stablr)
fit <- stabl(df, y = "response", n_bootstraps = 1000L, random_state = 42L)
fit                    # plain-language answer
get_feature_names(fit) # the selected features
plot(fit)              # stability paths + FDP+ curve
```

[`stabl_fit()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_fit.md)
exposes every argument — lambda grids, bootstrap design, thresholds,
learner adapters, sample grouping — and every accessor and workflow
applies to both objects. See
[`?stabl_fit`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_fit.md)
and the vignettes.

Everything beyond core STABL is labelled as an extension. Cooperative
fusion (Ding et al. 2022) ships on the vendored multiview engine for
gaussian and binomial families (Cox deferred). The random-forest learner
is calibrated for scoped settings: linear and nonlinear gaussian
problems with up to a few dozen predictors (`base_learner = "rf"`). The
ordinal learner is experimental pending its calibration study
(`base_learner = "ordinal"`). The environment-stability workflow
aggregates per-environment selections by their minimum frequency; it is
calibrated for small feature panels (see
[`?stabl_environment_stability`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_environment_stability.md)).

Interpretation limits are part of the contract. The fitted threshold is
the first minimizer of the observed FDP+ curve; a plotted `fdr_target`
is a visual reference, not a fitting target, and neither is a universal
false-discovery guarantee. Knockoff modes fail closed above 3,000
predictors because a globally valid chunked construction has not been
established; random-permutation controls remain available at larger
dimensions.

## Install

`stablr` compiles a C++17 native cooperative-learning backend at install
time. You need a C++17-capable compiler toolchain:

- **Windows:** [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/)
  (Rtools42 or later)
- **macOS:** Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`)
- **Linux:** GCC ≥ 7 or Clang ≥ 5 (usually pre-installed; install via
  `apt install r-base-dev` or equivalent)

### Install

``` r

# Install from GitHub
remotes::install_github("mdmanurung/stablr")

# Or from a local clone, from the repository root:
devtools::install_local(".")
```

### Dependencies

Optional functionality uses optional packages, in case these aren’t
installed automatically:

``` r

install.packages(c("ggplot2", "knockoff", "future", "furrr", "sparsegl"))
```

- `ggplot2`: plotting helpers and saved result figures
- `knockoff`: `artificial_type = "knockoff"`, `"knockoff_equi"`, or
  `"knockoff_mvr"`
- `future`, `furrr`: parallel bootstrap execution
- `sparsegl`: `base_learner = "sparse_group_lasso"`
- `mixOmics`: TCGA vignette dataset

plain-language selection out.

  STABL Stability Selection (Beginner Interface)

## Core STABL Engine

Fit single-matrix STABL selectors and compute FDP+ thresholds (expert
interface).

- [`stabl_fit()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_fit.md)
  [`print(`*`<stabl_fit>`*`)`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_fit.md)
  : Fit STABL (Stability-Penalized Feature Selection)
- [`auto_lambda_grid()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/auto_lambda_grid.md)
  : Build a Data-Driven Lambda Grid
- [`compute_fdp_plus()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/compute_fdp_plus.md)
  : Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound)

## Learner Grid Helpers

Data-driven threshold/lambda grid constructors for the non-glmnet base
learners. The random forest is calibrated within a measured scope
(WS-2); the ordinal learner is experimental (WS-9); sPLS-DA is
experimental and binomial-only. Learner factories are internal; select
learners via the `base_learner` argument of
[`stabl_fit()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_fit.md).

- [`auto_rf_threshold_grid()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/auto_rf_threshold_grid.md)
  : Auto-Generate an Importance-Threshold Grid for Random-Forest STABL
  (Experimental)
- [`auto_ordinal_lambda_grid()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/auto_ordinal_lambda_grid.md)
  : Build a Data-Driven Lambda Grid for the Ordinal Learner
  (Experimental)
- [`auto_splsda_keepx_grid()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/auto_splsda_keepx_grid.md)
  : Build an Automatic keepX Grid for the sPLS-DA Learner

## Environment Stability

ICP-inspired transportability workflow across environments (batches,
cohorts, sites); promoted with a documented scope after the WS-5
transportability benchmark (min-aggregation is the calibrated read).

- [`stabl_environment_stability()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/stabl_environment_stability.md)
  : Environment-Stability Workflow: Reliable and Transportable Feature
  Sets
- [`get_min_scores()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/get_min_scores.md)
  : Get Minimum-Across-Environment Stability Scores
- [`print(`*`<stabl_env_stability>`*`)`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/stablr/reference/print.stabl_env_stability.md)
  : Print an Environment-Stability Analysis
